To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) WGS is a powerful tool to identify risk for common disease; (b) WGS can be integrated with clinical data to provide more comprehensive risk assessment for individuals; and (c) WGS can provide a foundation for personalized wellness programs.

we have identified a set of eight sub-classes that are useful for visualizing the health risks associated with an individual's genome and that the concordance between the genetic risk and observed disease status for a set of four common conditions is approximately 2:1.

1) whole genome sequencing can be used to identify individuals who are at high risk for developing common complex diseases; 2) whole genome sequencing is useful in combination with traditional clinical evaluation for assessment of health risks; and 3) whole genome sequencing may be useful in the development of wellness and health promotion programs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new paradigm of health maintenance and disease prevention, in which whole genome sequence data and other genomic information are integrated with clinical and behavioral information to support personalized medicine.
how whole genome sequencing can be used in support of wellness maintenance.
the development of methods for combining genetic, phenotypic and family history data for the purposes of assessing health risks and for the design of personalized wellness plans for individuals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WGS can be used in support of wellness by providing a comprehensive view of risk for a wide range (over 100) of diseases.
the integration of whole genome sequencing into preventive medicine can provide an individualized assessment of risk and a personalized approach to wellness and health maintenance.

the CHDWB is a unique and valuable resource for the development and validation of novel approaches for integrating clinical and genetic data for assessment of health risks and the promotion of wellness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CHDWB is an example of how WGS and clinical data can be integrated to inform wellness and health maintenance in a way that is both personalized and holistic.

the integration of genotypic and longitudinal clinical information can be used to assess generalized risks for health and wellness, and to assist individuals to make informed choices in the promotion of health and maintenance of good physical and mental health.
the integration of WGS into the clinical evaluation process can provide additional information that is useful in the promotion of good health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
whole genome sequencing can be used to provide a comprehensive and personalized risk assessment that can be used to guide wellness programs.
WGS can be integrated into clinical evaluation to provide additional information about risk for disease, and that this can be done in a manner that is both clinically meaningful and actionable.

whole genome sequencing can be used to inform wellness and health maintenance, but that the interpretation of WGS must be done in the context of the patient’s medical history, family history, and clinical profile.
